text: CHAPTER 29
speaker: Narrator

text: What She Wanted
speaker: Narrator
note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

text: Enhedu moved while the others were still listening to the knock that had answered from beneath the City.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik was staring at the new ridge rising under the skin of his palm. Ninsun was still translating the last line that had carved itself into the wall. Balag stood between them and the man in the alcove with the patient stillness of someone who had already decided the ground was wrong. For a few breaths no one watched her.
speaker: Narrator

text: She had spent her whole life noticing the exact moment when attention slipped. She used it the way other people used doors.
speaker: Narrator

text: The passage past the alcove narrowed at once. Walls pressed close enough that her shoulders brushed both sides. The torchlight behind her thinned, then vanished. She kept walking until the voices were gone, swallowed by stone the way everything in this place eventually got swallowed, and only then let herself stop.
speaker: Narrator

text: She did not take the journal. She took the question that had been sitting behind her teeth since the gatekeeper first said the word Payment.
speaker: Narrator

text: What will I possess when I leave this place?
speaker: Narrator
note: Internal thought; intimate, not voiced aloud.

text: She did not speak it aloud. She simply held the thought the way she had once held a lockpick—firm, quiet, without apology—and waited to see whether the City would answer a request that had never been asked of it in words.
speaker: Narrator

text: The air changed first.
speaker: Narrator

text: The stone against her back went warm, then soft, then absent. Blue sky opened overhead, so bright it hurt. She was walking through a gate of white stone veined with gold. Bronze doors stood open. Servants bowed. Above the entrance, cut deep enough to last a thousand years, her own name:
speaker: Narrator

text: ENHEDU.
speaker: Narrator
note: Written text (ledger/inscription/journal, not in Bel-iddin's hand). Cold, deliberate read.

text: The air smelled of clean cistern water. Caravans rolled past loaded with lapis and ivory. Men who had once looked through her now waited in line, hats in hand. A ring slid onto her finger, cool at first and then warm. A house north of the river. Walls high enough to keep the starving world outside where it belonged.
speaker: Narrator

text: A woman stood in the doorway of that house. For one strange second Enhedu did not recognize her—older, softer, safe in a way that felt like a foreign language. Then she understood. It was her.
speaker: Narrator

text: Coin was the one thing in the world that never pretended to love you first. It had all led here.
speaker: Narrator

text: Enhedu smiled.
speaker: Narrator

text: Then, somewhere behind her ribs, everything went quiet.
speaker: Narrator

text: The change arrived so fast she almost missed it under the noise of her own triumph. She was still standing in the palace. She could still see the gold, still price it out of habit—the ring worth a season's rent, the vase worth a man's life if sold to the right buyer. She knew the house was beautiful. She knew the people around her were powerful.
speaker: Narrator

text: She felt none of it.
speaker: Narrator

text: The fire that had carried her through every bad deal and every worse night—the thing that had kept her moving when moving was the only thing keeping her fed—had simply gone out, like someone had reached into her chest and pinched the wick.
speaker: Narrator

text: The vision folded.
speaker: Narrator

text: She was back in the narrow dark of the passage, a small golden figurine solid and cold in her open hand. She knew exactly what it was worth. She knew exactly how many throats would be cut for it. She looked at it the way she would look at a chipped cup.
speaker: Narrator

text: Nothing there worth the looking.
speaker: Narrator

text: That was when Zik found her. He appeared at the far end of the passage without sound, the way everything in this place had learned to move. His eyes went from the figurine to her face. Something in her expression told him more than either object did.
speaker: Narrator

text: Enhedu?
speaker: Zik

text: She turned toward him. For the first time since he had known her, she looked lost, and she hated that he was the one who got to see it.
speaker: Narrator

text: I know this matters,
speaker: Enhedu

speaker: Narrator

text: I saw the life I wanted. Money. A house. People who couldn't decide I was worthless because they'd never been able to afford me in the first place.
speaker: Enhedu

text: Her voice stayed level. Whatever was underneath it had gone completely flat.
speaker: Narrator
